At FurtherAI, code changes merged per engineer each day grew **about 5x**, while the revert rate stayed under half a percent. AI reviews **99%** of changes before a person does, but planning and review now take 70% of the time, so the team wants **engineers to own more decisions**.

The Secrets of the Ice team found **48 prehistoric arrows** this year; more than **100 arrowheads and arrow shafts** have been recovered from one ice patch over the years. They estimate most ice patches containing archaeological artefacts will have disappeared within the next **20 years**.

cards.title: GitHub Incident with Actions, Pages, and Webhooks

depth.text: GitHub had an **outage** that delayed **Actions**, Pages deployments, and webhook events before services recovered

Delays affected **Actions workflows**, Pages deployments, and webhook events; errors also affected **code search and live updates**. GitHub said affected services recovered after mitigation, and the incident was resolved.

cards.camps: Two camps: some blame free CI and want it separated from paid infrastructure; others say self-hosting or switching to Forgejo has reduced outages for them.

cards.title: Bunny CDN Security Incident

depth.text: bunny.net pulled a server after its provider reported **unauthorized access**, then began **replacing certificates**

The provider reported unauthorized access involving third-party server management software; bunny.net says it cut traffic to its Armenia node within **20 minutes**, preserved security logs, wiped the server and removed it. bunny.net's investigation found **no evidence** the node or its data were accessed, though it cannot rule that out; if access happened, temporarily cached content, Pull Zone configurations and TLS certificates on the server could have been exposed. **Managed certificates** for custom domains are being reissued in controlled batches, with completion expected by the end of October 31.

cards.camps: Two camps: some call Bunny's response prompt and competent; others say wiping the server likely destroyed evidence and reflects a poor incident-response plan.

Within 20 minutes, we…

glossary.backbenchers: Politicians outside the government’s top leadership, who often have less say in day-to-day decisions.
glossary.red-tapism: Too much paperwork and official procedure getting in the way of doing things.
glossary.incumbent: The person or group that already holds an elected position.
glossary.phishing: A scam that tricks someone into entering login details on a fake site.
glossary.red team: Security testers who pretend to attack a system to find weaknesses.
glossary.PII: Personally Identifiable Information: details that could identify someone, such as an email or phone number.
glossary.access controls: Rules about who can get into a system or see its information.
glossary.security through obscurity: Relying on a system's details staying hidden instead of making it safe even if those details become known.
glossary.legacy code: Older software code that is still in use and may be hard to change.
glossary.refactor: Reorganize code without changing what it does.
glossary.AI tokens: Small pieces of text an AI works with; the amount available limits how much it can handle.
glossary.E2E tests: End-to-end tests: checks that run through a complete task from start to finish.
glossary.TNG: Star Trek: The Next Generation: the Star Trek show that featured Captain Picard.
glossary.local storage: A small space in your browser where a site can save information for later visits.
glossary.emulator: A program that imitates another service so you can try your software without using the real one.
glossary.PowerPC: A processor family used in the Mac and Nintendo systems discussed here.
glossary.HFS: A disk format older Macs use to organize files and folders.
glossary.BFS: BeOS’s disk format, which can store extra details about files and search for them live.
glossary.POSIX: Portable Operating System Interface: shared rules for how Unix-like systems behave.
glossary.FOSS: Free and Open Source Software: apps whose code people can inspect, share, and change.
glossary.SDK: Software Development Kit: tools a company provides so people can make apps for its device.
glossary.kernel: A small program that carries out a calculation on a computer's graphics chip or processor.
glossary.fat binaries: Programs built to run on more than one kind of processor, so people don’t need a separate version for each.
glossary.AI-native: Designed so AI is a core part of how the work gets done.
glossary.CI: Continuous integration: automatic checks that run when developers change code, helping catch problems early.
glossary.PR: Pull request: a proposed code change shared so others can review it.
glossary.revert rate: How often a code change has to be undone after it was added.
glossary.LOC: Lines of code: a count of how many lines a program contains.
glossary.open-weight models: AI models whose learned settings are made available for others to use or change.
glossary.capex: Capital expenditure: money spent up front on equipment or building something.
glossary.IPO: Initial Public Offering: when a company first offers its shares for the public to buy.
glossary.S-1: A filing that gives investors details about a company's finances and share offering before an IPO.
glossary.tokens: Small pieces of text an AI counts as it reads or writes; they can affect how much a request costs.
glossary.liquidity: How easily someone can turn something they own into money they can spend.
glossary.commodity: A product people can buy from different sellers that works much the same either way.
glossary.webhook: A message one service sends another when something happens.
glossary.self-hosted: Running a service on a computer you control rather than relying on someone else's.
glossary.deployment: Putting an app or change into use so people can access it.
glossary.sandboxed app: An app kept within limits on what it can access on your computer.
glossary.Accessibility permissions: A Mac permission that lets an app use tools for interacting with the computer on someone's behalf.
glossary.local network permission: A setting that lets an app look for devices connected to the same network.
glossary.multicast discovery: A way for devices on the same network to announce themselves and find one another.
glossary.LAN: Local Area Network: devices connected to the same nearby network.
glossary.CDN: Content Delivery Network: A network of servers that helps websites handle requests closer to their users.
glossary.TLS certificate: Transport Layer Security certificate: a digital ID that helps a website prove it's the right site and set up a protected connection.
glossary.private key: A secret digital key that can be used to prove an identity or act as its owner.
glossary.Pull Zone: Bunny's settings that tell its CDN what website content to fetch and serve.
glossary.POP: Point of presence: a server location where a network's users can connect nearby.
glossary.LLM: Large Language Model: an AI trained on lots of writing so it can take written questions and produce written answers.
glossary.continual learning: An AI's ability to keep learning new things over time without losing what it already learned.
glossary.on-policy distillation: A way to train one AI using guidance from another AI on examples the first AI generated itself.
glossary.KV-cache: A saved record of what an AI has already processed, so it does not have to redo that work when generating more text.
glossary.MoE: Mixture of Experts: a model with many specialist parts that sends each piece of text to only a few of them.
glossary.RLHF: Reinforcement Learning from Human Feedback: a way to train an AI by having people rate its answers.
glossary.in-context learning: Getting an AI to do a task using examples or instructions in the current conversation, without changing what it learned earlier.
glossary.knowledge graph: A way to organize information by showing how people, places, or things are connected.
glossary.parameter expansion: Adding more adjustable values inside an AI so it has more room to learn new information.
glossary.remote code execution: A security flaw that lets someone run commands on another person's computer.
glossary.CVE: Common Vulnerabilities and Exposures: a standard ID assigned to a publicly known security flaw so people can refer to the same issue.
glossary.MPTCP: Multipath TCP: a way for one internet connection to use more than one network path.
glossary.Turnstile: Cloudflare’s check that a site can use to decide whether to let a visitor through.
glossary.headless browser: A browser that runs under software control without a visible window.
glossary.browser profile: A saved set of details that makes a browser act like a particular kind of browser.
glossary.cf_clearance cookie: A small piece of data saved by a browser; here, it shows that a Cloudflare challenge was cleared.
glossary.proxy: A go-between that gets information from another website on someone else's behalf.
glossary.user agent: A label sent with a web request that identifies the browser or device making it.
glossary.PoW: Proof of Work: a computer task that makes automated requests take some effort.
